thoughts.name: Gluttony
thoughts.summary: The pull of food, drink and comfort, and the reasonable-sounding excuses that come with it. Evagrius starts here because this thought opens the door to the others.

thoughts.name: Fornication
thoughts.summary: Sexual temptation in fantasy, memory and desire, along with the shame and discouragement that follow a fall.

clusters.title: At night, and in the body

thoughts.name: Love of money
thoughts.summary: Anxiety about having enough, the urge to hold on to what you have, and envy of what other people own.

clusters.title: Afraid of losing or running out
Holding back from people in need

thoughts.name: Sadness
thoughts.summary: Grief, dread, and the feeling that God is far away or that nothing will ever change.

thoughts.name: Anger
thoughts.summary: Irritation, grudges, and replaying the ways other people have wronged you.

thoughts.name: Listlessness (acedia)
thoughts.summary: Boredom, restlessness, and the urge to quit or be somewhere else: the “noonday demon.”

clusters.title: Pulled back to home and the world

thoughts.name: Vainglory
thoughts.summary: Wanting to be seen, praised and admired, even for doing good.

clusters.title: Wanting to be seen and admired

thoughts.name: Pride
thoughts.summary: Believing you did it all yourself, looking down on others, and needing no one’s help, not even God’s.

entries.voice: I want to grow spiritually without the hard part.
entries.situation: Wanting the harvest of a disciplined life without the work of self-denial.
entries.note: In the Greek Bible Evagrius read, Issachar sees that the land is good and bends his shoulder to farm it.

passages.text: “Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags. He saw a resting place, that it was good, the land, that it was pleasant. He bows his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a servant doing forced labor.

greek.text: Issachar has desired that which is good; resting between the inheritances. And having seen the resting place that it was good, and the land that it was fertile, he subjected his shoulder to labour, and became a husbandman.

entries.voice: Fasting gets you nothing. It won’t make you any holier.
entries.situation: Doubting that self-denial does your soul any real good.
entries.note: Evagrius’s Greek text says the bronze washing basin was made from the mirrors of women who fasted at the tent’s door. Their discipline became part of God’s house.

passages.text: He made the basin of bronze, and its base of bronze, out of the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

greek.text: He made the brazen laver, and the brazen base of it of the mirrors of the women that fasted, who fasted by the doors of the tabernacle of witness, in the day in which he set it up.

entries.voice: It’s a special day, and you’re run down anyway. Indulge.
entries.situation: Using a holiday or feeling unwell as the reason to give in to a craving.

passages.text: …You will not eat just one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days, but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils, and it is loathsome to you; because you have rejected the LORD who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”

entries.voice: Eat until you’re full. What harm could it do?
entries.situation: Filling up without noticing how comfort makes you forget God.

passages.text: …you shall eat and be full; then beware lest you forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

entries.voice: God asks too much. Fasting is a burden.
entries.situation: Feeling that God’s call to self-control is too heavy for you.

passages.text: For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant.

greek.text: For this command which I give thee this day is not grievous, neither is it far from thee.

entries.voice: Food and drink can’t hurt your soul.
entries.situation: Assuming indulgence has no effect on your life with God.

passages.text: But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat. You have grown thick. You have become sleek. Then he abandoned God who made him, and rejected the Rock of his salvation.

entries.voice: You’ve fasted long enough. Eat now. Don’t wait for evening.
entries.situation: Wanting to break a fast before the time you set.
entries.note: Desert monks usually ate in mid-afternoon (the “ninth hour”). Here the pull is to eat at the usual time on a day set aside for a longer fast.

passages.text: All the people came to urge David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David swore, saying, “God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or anything else, until the sun goes down.”

entries.voice: You’re going to run out of what you need.
entries.situation: Fear that your food, money or supplies are about to run dry.

passages.text: For the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that the LORD sends rain on the earth.’”

entries.voice: I can follow the saints and keep every comfort too.
entries.situation: Wanting a holy life without giving anything up.
entries.note: Micaiah told the king the truth and was given the “bread of affliction” for it.

passages.text: The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king’s son. Say, ‘The king says, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.”’”

entries.voice: There isn’t enough to share with everyone who comes.
entries.situation: Holding back hospitality because you’re afraid there won’t be enough.

passages.text: His servant said, “What, should I set this before a hundred men?” But he said, “Give it to the people, that they may eat; for the LORD says, ‘They will eat, and will have some left over.’” So he set it before them and they ate and had some left over, according to the LORD’s word.

entries.voice: Living with this little is bitter. You deserve better.
entries.situation: Resentment about being poor or having little.

passages.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.

entries.voice: Better stock up on more. For guests, of course.
entries.situation: Hoarding more than you need and calling it hospitality.

passages.text: I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his children begging for bread.

entries.voice: Worry about what to eat and wear. The truth can wait.
entries.situation: Busy with food and clothes while ignoring what is wrong in your heart.

passages.text: For I will declare my iniquity. I will be sorry for my sin.

entries.voice: Ease up. All this fasting and work will wear out your body.
entries.situation: Being told your discipline is too hard on your weak body.

passages.text: that he should live on forever, that he should not see corruption.

greek.text: …though he labour for ever, and live to the end, so that he should not see corruption.

entries.voice: Don’t push yourself so hard staying up to pray.
entries.situation: Pressure to drop the late-night or early-morning prayer you committed to.

passages.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.

entries.voice: Where is your next meal coming from? You’d better figure it out.
entries.situation: Anxious scheming about how to get food, drink or money.

passages.text: Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.

entries.voice: Staying awake to pray just stirs up more thoughts.
entries.situation: Feeling that praying at night only brings more distraction.

passages.text: I watch, and have become like a sparrow that is alone on the housetop.

entries.voice: Giving that up is ridiculous. Nobody lives like that.
entries.situation: Being mocked or second-guessed for giving something up.

passages.text: My knees are weak through fasting. My body is thin and lacks fat.

entries.voice: Keep fasting like this and you’ll ruin your health.
entries.situation: Fear that your discipline will harm you, or even kill you.

passages.text: I will not die, but live, and declare the LORD’s works.

entries.voice: Skip prayer tonight. Your body needs the rest.
entries.situation: Talking yourself out of a prayer commitment for the sake of comfort.

passages.text: “Surely I will not come into the structure of my house, nor go up into my bed; I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids, until I find out a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”

entries.voice: Hard times are coming. You won’t make it.
entries.situation: Dread that famine, recession or disaster is just around the corner.

passages.text: The LORD will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.

entries.voice: Have a drink. Water alone isn’t good for you.
entries.situation: Justifying alcohol as healthier than going without.
entries.note: This line appears only in the Greek version of Proverbs.

greek.text: He that enjoys himself in banquets of wine, shall leave dishonour in his own strong holds.

entries.voice: Plan your next meal. Growing in virtue can wait.
entries.situation: Thinking more about food than about becoming a better person.

passages.text: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.

greek.text: With every one who is careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in want.

entries.voice: Plain food again? This is miserable.
entries.situation: Complaining about simple meals.

passages.text: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

entries.voice: It’s a holiday. Be kind to yourself and have something nice.
entries.situation: Treating a celebration as permission to indulge.

passages.text: Delicate living is not appropriate for a fool, much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

greek.text: Delight does not suit a fool, nor is it seemly if a servant should begin to rule with haughtiness.

entries.voice: You’ll get stomach trouble without a little wine.
entries.situation: Inventing health reasons to drink when you aren’t sick.

passages.text: Wine is a mocker and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

greek.text: Wine is an intemperate thing, and strong drink full of violence: but every fool is entangled with them.

entries.voice: Swear you’ll never eat that again. Make a vow.
entries.situation: Binding yourself with rash vows about fasting or dieting.

passages.text: It is a snare to a man to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his vows.

greek.text: It is a snare to a man hastily to consecrate some of his own property: for in that case repentance comes after vowing.

entries.voice: They can get help somewhere else. It’s not your job.
entries.situation: Holding back food or help from someone in need.

passages.text: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

greek.text: He that has pity on the poor shall himself be maintained; for he has given of his own bread to the poor.

entries.voice: You almost never indulge. Once in a long while is fine.
entries.situation: A gentle suggestion that a rare binge doesn’t count.

passages.text: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat; for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.

greek.text: Be not a wine-bibber, neither continue long at feasts, and purchases of flesh: for every drunkard and whoremonger shall be poor; and every sluggard shall clothe himself with tatters and ragged garments.

entries.voice: Remember those great evenings with good wine?
entries.situation: Nostalgia for past drinking and good times at the table.

passages.text: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly. In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.

greek.text: For if thou shouldest set thine eyes on bowls and cups, thou shalt afterwards go more naked than a pestle. But at last such a one stretches himself out as one smitten by a serpent, and venom is diffused through him as by a horned serpent.

entries.voice: Fill your stomach, even if it’s only bread and water.
entries.situation: The urge to eat until you are full, even of simple food.
entries.note: The source of this quotation is uncertain. It closely matches the Greek of Proverbs 24:15.

greek.text: Bring not an ungodly man into the dwelling of the righteous: neither be deceived by the feeding of the belly.

entries.voice: You’d be embarrassed not to go along with them.
entries.situation: Pressure to drop a commitment because refusing feels awkward in front of people you respect.
entries.note: The text of this entry may be damaged in the manuscripts. The verse distinguishes good shame from bad.

passages.text: For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace.

entries.voice: You’ve been strict for so long. Food can’t hurt you now.
entries.situation: Flattering promises that you’ve earned the right to indulge freely.

passages.text: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.

greek.text: A weeping enemy promises all things with his lips, but in his heart he contrives deceit.

entries.voice: God’s commands only bring you hardship and misery.
entries.situation: Seeing God’s commands as harsh rather than loving.

passages.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

entries.voice: Wine was made for people. Enjoy it.
entries.situation: Arguing that a good gift is always meant to be used right now.

passages.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.

entries.voice: Go back to how things used to be: the parties, the drinks.
entries.situation: Longing to return to old habits of feasting and drinking.

passages.text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.

entries.voice: Go further. Live rough, cut everyone off, prove your devotion.
entries.situation: Being pushed toward extreme austerity and isolation beyond what is wise.

passages.text: Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

greek.text: Be not very just; neither be very wise: lest thou be confounded.

entries.voice: Remember how good life used to be? Look at it now.
entries.situation: Comparing a hard present with comfortable memories.

passages.text: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.

entries.voice: Picture the full table back home with family.
entries.situation: Daydreaming about a place of comfort and plenty you have left behind.

passages.text: Arise, and depart! For this is not your resting place, because of uncleanness that destroys, even with a grievous destruction.

entries.voice: Everyone else is feasting and celebrating without you.
entries.situation: Feeling left out while others enjoy food and celebration.

passages.text: yet I will rejoice in the LORD. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!

entries.voice: A life of pleasure is better than this life of faith.
entries.situation: Calling indulgence good and the way of discipline bad.

passages.text: Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

entries.voice: I’m so tired of going without.
entries.situation: Weariness after a long stretch of having little.

passages.text: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers; and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”

entries.voice: My body is worn out, and my mind is full of impure thoughts.
entries.situation: Physically drained and still tempted, and asking God to remember you.

passages.text: LORD, you know. Remember me, visit me, and avenge me of my persecutors. You are patient, so don’t take me away. Know that for your sake I have suffered reproach.

entries.voice: I feel weak and sick, like I’m wasting away.
entries.situation: Sudden physical weakness and distress, brought to God.

passages.text: “Look, LORD; for I am in distress. My heart is troubled. My heart turns over within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad, the sword bereaves. At home, it is like death.

entries.voice: Bread and water aren’t enough. I want something more.
entries.situation: Not content with simple food and wanting extras.

passages.text: …Test your servants, I beg you, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink. Then let our faces be examined before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s delicacies; and as you see, deal with your servants.” So he listened to them in this matter, and tested them for ten days. At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer and they were fatter in flesh than all the youths who ate of the king’s delicacies. So the steward took away their delicacies and the wine that they were given to drink, and gave them vegetables.

entries.voice: How can I stand firm when temptation hits?
entries.situation: Looking for strength against temptation. Jesus prepared by fasting.

passages.text: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.

entries.voice: You have to worry. Guests, illness and hard times are coming.
entries.situation: Anxiety about food and clothing dressed up as being responsible.

passages.text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

entries.voice: Treat yourself well and life will go well.
entries.situation: Believing that comfort and pleasure are the road to a good life.

passages.text: How narrow is the gate and the way is restricted that leads to life! There are few who find it.

entries.voice: There’s not enough for both of you, and they’re probably lazy anyway.
entries.situation: Finding reasons not to share with someone in need.

passages.text: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”

entries.voice: Look after yourself first. Keep it for you.
entries.situation: Gathering food and goods for yourself alone.

passages.text: All who believed were together, and had all things in common. They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need.

entries.voice: This hardship is wearing me down.
entries.situation: Growing weary under the strain of self-restraint.

passages.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.

entries.voice: Take care of yourself. Eat and drink a little more.
entries.situation: Using self-care as cover for indulging.

passages.text: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.

entries.voice: Just a small treat. It’s only something little.
entries.situation: Wanting a small comfort food to console yourself.
entries.note: For desert monks who lived on bread and water, cooked vegetables were a treat.

passages.text: One man has faith to eat all things, but he who is weak eats only vegetables.

entries.voice: It’s the season for it. You have to have some.
entries.situation: Seasonal cravings that feel impossible to pass up.

passages.text: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.

entries.voice: You’re in real need. Ease off; you can’t keep this up.
entries.situation: Hardship slowly draining your resolve.

passages.text: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair; pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed; always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

entries.voice: Your stomach, your liver… something is seriously wrong.
entries.situation: Imagining illness and fixating on symptoms.

passages.text: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.

entries.voice: Your body is falling apart.
entries.situation: Distress as your body ages or declines.

passages.text: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.

entries.voice: Why did you give that away? You’ll regret it.
entries.situation: Regret or annoyance after being generous.

passages.text: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

greek.text: …God loves a cheerful and liberal man; but a man shall fully prove the folly of his works. He that has pity on the poor shall himself be maintained; for he has given of his own bread to the poor.

entries.voice: You’ll make yourself sick. Eat a proper meal.
entries.situation: Fear of weakness used to make you break a commitment.

passages.text: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

entries.voice: It’s a celebration. Get a little drunk.
entries.situation: Wanting to drink heavily on a holiday or special occasion.

passages.text: Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit, speaking to one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs; singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;

entries.voice: Don’t work for it, and don’t ask family. Let others cover you.
entries.situation: Anxious maneuvering about how your needs will be met.

passages.text: Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand. In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

entries.voice: You’ll go hungry, or worse, have to accept charity.
entries.situation: Fear of need, and of the humiliation of receiving help.

passages.text: I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

entries.voice: Why work with your hands? Others will provide.
entries.situation: Avoiding honest work and expecting others to support you.

passages.text: …that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you, that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and may have need of nothing.

entries.voice: Skip the work. Just eat and fill up.
entries.situation: Wanting comfort without contributing anything.

passages.text: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.”

entries.voice: This discipline is cruel and does nothing for your soul.
entries.situation: Feeling that a disciplined life is all pain and no gain.

passages.text: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

entries.voice: Focus on your meals. Other people’s needs aren’t your problem.
entries.situation: Caring about your own food while neglecting people in need.

passages.text: But don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

entries.voice: Even Paul told Timothy to drink a little wine.
entries.situation: Quoting Scripture to justify drinking when you aren’t ill.
entries.note: Paul’s advice was for Timothy’s frequent illnesses. Evagrius aims the verse at a thought that borrows the permission without the illness.

passages.text: Lay hands hastily on no one. Don’t be a participant in other people’s sins. Keep yourself pure. Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities.

entries.voice: Go back to the world and its ways. They’re not so bad.
entries.situation: Being drawn back toward the world’s way of living.

passages.text: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

entries.voice: Fasting is too hard. God can’t really expect this.
entries.situation: Feeling that self-denial is an impossible burden.

passages.text: For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous. For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.

entries.voice: Picture her. She’s married, but it’s only a thought.
entries.situation: Fantasizing about someone who belongs to another.

passages.text: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”

entries.voice: After all this struggle, what good is waiting for you?
entries.situation: Discouraged that years of resisting temptation seem to have earned nothing.

passages.text: But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries. For my angel shall go before you, and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I will cut them off.

entries.voice: This should be gone in an instant. If it isn’t, something’s wrong.
entries.situation: Expecting instant freedom, and losing heart when progress is slow.

passages.text: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you. Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

entries.voice: You’re young. You can’t possibly keep your mind pure.
entries.situation: Believing purity is impossible at your age.
entries.note: Evagrius reads this verse as proof that the young, too, can bring God a clean offering.

passages.text: Everyone who passes over to those who are counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering to the LORD.

entries.voice: You’re young. It doesn’t count yet.
entries.situation: Excusing sexual sin or impure thoughts because of your age.

passages.text: The LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot him out of my book.

entries.voice: It’s only in my head. I can play it out there.
entries.situation: Entertaining a fantasy instead of guarding your mind.

passages.text: Hear therefore, Israel, and observe to do it, that it may be well with you, and that you may increase mightily, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.

entries.voice: Go toward it. Just see where the desire leads.
entries.situation: Drifting toward lust as if it were something worth serving.

passages.text: You shall fear the LORD your God; and you shall serve him, and shall swear by his name.

entries.voice: It’s day and night. I’ll never beat this.
entries.situation: Constant temptation wearing away your hope of victory.

passages.text: If you shall say in your heart, “These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?” you shall not be afraid of them. You shall remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

entries.voice: One picture after another, until one finally sticks.
entries.situation: A mind cycling through images until one takes hold.

passages.text: Know therefore today that the LORD your God is he who goes over before you as a devouring fire. He will destroy them and he will bring them down before you. So you shall drive them out and make them perish quickly, as the LORD has spoken to you.

entries.voice: The temptation is gone. You’ve made it. Relax.
entries.situation: Easing your guard during a lull, as if the battle were over.

passages.text: You shall not do all the things that we do here today, every man whatever is right in his own eyes; for you haven’t yet come to the rest and to the inheritance which the LORD your God gives you.

entries.voice: I feel it in my body, and it frightens me.
entries.situation: Fear when temptation is felt physically.

passages.text: You are happy, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency? Your enemies will submit themselves to you. You will tread on their high places.”

entries.voice: I’m too low to keep fighting these thoughts.
entries.situation: Sadness draining the strength to resist impure thoughts during prayer.

passages.text: Deborah said to Barak, “Go; for this is the day in which the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Hasn’t the LORD gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

entries.voice: I’ll fight it, but not all the way. I can shake free anytime.
entries.situation: Keeping a little of the temptation around, sure you can walk away whenever you like.

passages.text: She said, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” He awoke out of his sleep, and said, “I will go out as at other times, and shake myself free.” But he didn’t know that the LORD had departed from him. The Philistines laid hold on him and put out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with fetters of bronze; and he ground at the mill in the prison.

entries.voice: The temptation suddenly lifted. Thank God.
