entries.situation: Not seeing that weak faith breeds fear.

passages.text: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.

entries.voice: I’ve been humiliated for following Jesus.
entries.situation: Sad about being dishonored for your faith.

passages.text: They therefore departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for Jesus’ name.

entries.voice: This suffering is meaningless.
entries.situation: Suffering that seems to come from temptation and serve no purpose.

passages.text: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance; and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope; and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

entries.voice: Terrible suffering lies ahead of you.
entries.situation: Predictions of severe suffering to come.

passages.text: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us.

entries.voice: This is more than I can take.
entries.situation: Believing you’re being tested beyond your strength.

passages.text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

entries.voice: This trial is beyond words. I feel like I’m dying.
entries.situation: An overwhelming trial you can’t even describe.

passages.text: Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead, who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver, on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us,

entries.voice: Remember what you did when you were young?
entries.situation: The sins of your youth brought back to shame you.

passages.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

entries.voice: Losing this is crushing you, and it should.
entries.situation: Grief over passing, worldly things sinking your mind.

passages.text: For godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.

entries.voice: You’re in open war now, and you’ll lose.
entries.situation: Thoughts that come when the struggle is out in the open.

passages.text: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

entries.voice: You’ll be wounded, and your body will never recover.
entries.situation: Fear of lasting harm and incurable illness.

passages.text: Now who will harm you if you become imitators of that which is good? But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.” But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. …

entries.voice: There’s bad blood between us. Nothing can fix it now.
entries.situation: Not realizing that a gift can soften a long-standing grudge.
entries.note: Jacob met his estranged brother Esau with gifts, and the old enmity melted.

passages.text: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me. Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.

entries.voice: You’re doing the right thing. You’re allowed to be angry about it.
entries.situation: Irritation that flares up even while you’re trying to live rightly.

passages.text: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”

entries.voice: Twist the story a little. They deserve it.
entries.situation: Anger tempting you to misrepresent someone.

passages.text: “You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.

entries.voice: Did you hear what they said about you?
entries.situation: Rage stirred up by gossip or a secondhand report.

passages.text: “You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.

greek.text: Thou shalt not receive a vain report: thou shalt not agree with the unjust man to become an unjust witness.

entries.voice: Tell them exactly what you think of them.
entries.situation: Wanting to lash out at someone with insults.

passages.text: “Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous; for I will not justify the wicked.

greek.text: Thou shalt abstain from every unjust thing: thou shalt not slay the innocent and just, and thou shalt not justify the wicked for gifts.

entries.voice: Remember the hateful thing they said?
entries.situation: Replaying the scene of someone speaking against you.
entries.note: Evagrius quotes John of Thebes: hatred over money or food can fade, but hatred over honor and reputation is hard to uproot.

passages.text: “‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.

entries.voice: No one can really be that humble. It’s not human.
entries.situation: Believing true gentleness and humility are impossible.

passages.text: Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.

entries.voice: How dare they insult me like that?
entries.situation: Not seeing that insults can be a test God permits.
entries.note: When Shimei cursed King David, David refused to strike back: perhaps the LORD would see his distress and repay him with good.

passages.text: David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my son, who came out of my bowels, seeks my life. How much more this Benjamite, now? Leave him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD has invited him. It may be that the LORD will look on the wrong done to me, and that the LORD will repay me good for the cursing of me today.”

entries.voice: I want to know God’s ways, but I won’t be humbled.
entries.situation: Wanting to grow in faith while skipping humility.

passages.text: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.

entries.voice: They’re up to something. Add it to the list.
entries.situation: Collecting suspicions and pretexts against people.

passages.text: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don’t fret; it leads only to evildoing. For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD shall inherit the land.

entries.voice: Listen to what everyone is saying about them.
entries.situation: Slander about someone clouding your mind with rage.

passages.text: You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son.

entries.voice: My nights are troubled, and I think my anger is the cause.
entries.situation: Discovering that rage feeds bad nights, and mercy and patience calm them.
entries.note: Evagrius noticed that frightening dreams often come from the turmoil of anger, and fade through mercy and patience.

passages.text: Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for your commandments are always with me. I have more understanding than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation.

entries.voice: Sing about patience. You’re furious, but sing it anyway.
entries.situation: Feeling like a hypocrite praying words you aren’t living.

passages.text: How can we sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land?

entries.voice: They’re lazy, rude, and never do what they should.
entries.situation: Building a case against someone in your head.

passages.text: Don’t devise evil against your neighbor, since he dwells securely by you.

entries.voice: Fight them on this. It matters.
entries.situation: Wanting to quarrel over things that won’t last.

passages.text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.

entries.voice: Curse them. They’ve earned it.
entries.situation: Wanting to call down harm on someone.

passages.text: He who hides hatred has lying lips. He who utters a slander is a fool.

greek.text: Righteous lips cover enmity; but they that utter railings are most foolish.

entries.voice: I can’t pray. I’m still furious with them.
entries.situation: Anger at someone spoiling your prayer.

passages.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.

greek.text: Every sincere soul is blessed: but a passionate man is not graceful.

entries.voice: This stupid animal won’t do what I want!
entries.situation: Losing your temper with an animal, or anything that won’t cooperate.

passages.text: A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

greek.text: A righteous man has pity for the lives of his cattle; but the bowels of the ungodly are unmerciful.

entries.voice: That’s it. That tiny thing was the last straw.
entries.situation: Flaring up over something trivial.

passages.text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.

entries.voice: Set a trap for them. They’ll never see it coming.
entries.situation: Plotting something underhanded against someone.

passages.text: The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.

greek.text: A deceitful man shall catch no game; but a blameless man is a precious possession.

entries.voice: Replay it again. Remember exactly what they said.
entries.situation: Resentment that keeps an old word alive long after the anger cools.

passages.text: In the way of righteousness is life; in its path there is no death.

greek.text: In the ways of righteousness is life; but the ways of those that remember injuries lead to death.

entries.voice: Forget patience. React now.
entries.situation: Anger uprooting your patience and pushing you to foolish acts.

passages.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.

greek.text: A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish.

entries.voice: Who are they to correct me?
entries.situation: Anger at being rightly corrected.

passages.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

entries.voice: Don’t let it go. Win the argument.
entries.situation: Being drawn into strife and unable to drop an argument.

passages.text: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.

entries.voice: It’s only a thought. As long as I don’t act on it, it’s fine.
entries.situation: Believing angry thoughts don’t matter, only actions.

passages.text: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.

entries.voice: Hang around with the angry ones. They tell it like it is.
entries.situation: Drawn to angry people and heated talk.

passages.text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger, lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.

entries.voice: They did it to me. I’ll do it right back.
entries.situation: Wanting to hurt someone the way they hurt you.

passages.text: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”

greek.text: Say not, As he has treated me, so will I treat him, and I will avenge myself on him for that wherein he has injured me.

entries.voice: Let my enemy go hungry. Serves them right.
entries.situation: Refusing kindness to someone who is against you, even in their need.

passages.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink; for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and the LORD will reward you.

entries.voice: I’m boiling. Everyone is getting on my nerves.
entries.situation: Quick to flare up and grow bitter with people.

passages.text: Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.

entries.voice: I have every reason to be angry, and I’m keeping them.
entries.situation: Clinging to reasons for anger rooted in comfort, wealth or status.

passages.text: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.

entries.voice: After all this, how can you still love them?
entries.situation: Trials wearing down your love for others.

passages.text: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.

entries.voice: Write them a message that will really sting.
entries.situation: Wanting to send hurtful words to someone who troubled you.

passages.text: Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees

entries.voice: The anger that used to grip me has let go.
entries.situation: Thanking God that old anger no longer provokes you.

passages.text: Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul. You have redeemed my life. LORD, you have seen my wrong. Judge my cause. You have seen all their vengeance and all their plans against me.

entries.voice: My own family attacks my faith, and I’m furious.
entries.situation: Anger at family who oppose you for following Christ.

passages.text: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.voice: I’m restless and bored, and they’re irritating me.
entries.situation: Restlessness turning into irritation with someone.

passages.text: But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause will be in danger of the judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’ will be in danger of the council. Whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.

entries.voice: They hurt me again. Now I’ll never let it go.
entries.situation: A second offense locking in resentment from the first.

passages.text: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.

entries.voice: Hate them. Curse them. They’re your enemy.
entries.situation: Thoughts pushing you to hate and curse your enemies.

passages.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you, that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.

entries.voice: They apologized? Not good enough.
entries.situation: Refusing to accept someone’s repentance.

passages.text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him. If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”

entries.voice: Love one another? Not them.
entries.situation: Anger bending the command to love into something smaller.

passages.text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.

entries.voice: I’m too bitter to love anyone right now.
entries.situation: Anger hardening into bitterness against love itself.

passages.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

entries.voice: Good. They’re suffering. They deserve it.
entries.situation: Secret pleasure at an enemy’s misfortune.

passages.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep. Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.

entries.voice: I won’t forget this. One day I’ll pay them back.
entries.situation: Holding a grudge and waiting to repay evil.

passages.text: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.

entries.voice: Take what you’re owed. Cheat them back if you have to.
entries.situation: Anger pushing you to take advantage of someone.

passages.text: …Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded? No, but you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that against your brothers.

entries.voice: They mocked my station in life. I won’t stand for it.
entries.situation: Enraged when someone mocks your job, class or circumstances.

passages.text: Were you called being a bondservant? Don’t let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it. For he who was called in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord’s free man. Likewise he who was called being free is Christ’s bondservant.

entries.voice: I can’t speak openly with them anymore.
entries.situation: Anger shutting down the honest, loving speech you once had.

passages.text: …Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil; doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things. …

entries.voice: I want deep spiritual insight, though I lose my temper easily.
entries.situation: Seeking spiritual depth while staying quick-tempered.

passages.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

entries.voice: Their failures drive me crazy.
entries.situation: Grieved and annoyed by other people’s failings.

passages.text: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

entries.voice: After all I did for them, they complain?
entries.situation: Anger at someone who is ungrateful for your kindness.

passages.text: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.

entries.voice: Don’t make peace. They’ll only do it again.
entries.situation: Shame, fear and pride disguised as reasons not to reconcile.
entries.note: Evagrius calls this the demon’s craftiness: it dresses up shame, fear and pride as sensible reasons.

passages.text: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.

entries.voice: So many things make me angry.
entries.situation: Anger spilling over into every kind of thought.

passages.text: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice.

entries.voice: Why am I always the one serving everyone?
entries.situation: Grumbling about serving others.

passages.text: Do all things without complaining and arguing, that you may become blameless and harmless, children of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you are seen as lights in the world,

entries.voice: I’m so angry I could say anything, even about God.
entries.situation: Heated anger giving birth to blasphemy or deceit.

passages.text: but now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and shameful speaking out of your mouth. Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,

entries.voice: Evil for evil. That’s only fair.
entries.situation: Wanting to repay harm with harm.

passages.text: See that no one returns evil for evil to anyone, but always follow after that which is good for one another and for all.

entries.voice: God’s commands are about being right, not about love.
entries.situation: Anger twisting faith away from its goal of love.

passages.text: But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith,

entries.voice: I keep arguing with them in my head.
entries.situation: Imaginary arguments stirring up conflict in your mind.

passages.text: The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient,

entries.voice: My relatives turned on me because I follow Christ.
entries.situation: Anger at being persecuted by family for your faith.

passages.text: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.

entries.voice: They owe me, and they aren’t even trying to repay.
entries.situation: Anger at someone who hasn’t paid you back.

passages.text: But if he has wronged you at all or owes you anything, put that to my account.

entries.voice: I want to be righteous, but I snap at people.
entries.situation: Seeking God’s righteousness while angering quickly.

passages.text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

entries.voice: I’m full of anger, but I want God’s wisdom.
entries.situation: Wanting wisdom while your mind is full of anger.

passages.text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

entries.voice: That rule against speaking ill of others isn’t fair.
entries.situation: Defending slander by questioning God’s law.

passages.text: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge. Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

entries.voice: Insult for insult. Don’t bless them.
entries.situation: Refusing to answer abuse with blessing.

passages.text: not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.

entries.voice: I fear God. I just can’t stand that person.
entries.situation: Claiming devotion while hating someone.

passages.text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness even until now.

entries.voice: I wish they were gone.
entries.situation: Hatred that turns murderous in the mind.

passages.text: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.

entries.voice: I love God. I just don’t love them anymore.
entries.situation: Saying you love God while hatred has replaced your love for someone.

passages.text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?

entries.voice: This work is so tedious. Find an easier job that pays better.
entries.situation: Restless dislike of your daily work, and the urge to switch to something easier.

passages.text: You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, for you were taken out of it. For you are dust, and you shall return to dust.”

entries.voice: Your leader is harsh and never shows anyone mercy.
entries.situation: Restlessness turning into criticism of the people in charge.

passages.text: “You shall not blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of your people.

entries.voice: Where’s the payoff? I should be seeing results by now.
entries.situation: Impatience for spiritual fruit that hasn’t come yet.

passages.text: …Be courageous, and bring some of the fruit of the land. …

greek.text: …and ye shall persevere and take of the fruits of the land…

entries.voice: The world looks more appealing than this.
entries.situation: Restlessness turning your heart back toward the world.

passages.text: Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God. The LORD is one. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.

entries.voice: You don’t need to read Scripture. Some saints barely knew any.
entries.situation: Excusing yourself from reading and learning God’s word.

passages.text: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart; and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.

entries.voice: I feel a little unwell, so nothing’s worth doing.
entries.situation: A minor ailment draining all your motivation.

passages.text: The LORD will take away from you all sickness; and he will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you know, on you, but will lay them on all those who hate you.

entries.voice: I miss my family. This restlessness is stronger than me.
entries.situation: Homesick and convinced you can’t beat the restlessness.

passages.text: The LORD will cause your enemies who rise up against you to be struck before you. They will come out against you one way, and will flee before you seven ways.

entries.voice: Skip the reading. Just ask God to teach you directly.
entries.situation: Avoiding Scripture with a spiritual-sounding excuse.

passages.text: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”

entries.voice: Why does God let me be tested like this, irritated by everyone?
entries.situation: Asking why God allows the trials that make you irritable and sad.

passages.text: …that by them I may test Israel, to see if they will keep the LORD’s way to walk therein, as their fathers kept it, or not.” So the LORD left those nations, without driving them out hastily. He didn’t deliver them into Joshua’s hand. Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to test Israel by them, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan; only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war…

entries.voice: I won’t cry. Tears won’t help.
entries.situation: A hardened heart that refuses the relief of tears.
entries.note: Evagrius calls tears a great remedy for restless, troubled nights.

passages.text: I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.

entries.voice: This restlessness won’t leave me.
entries.situation: Persistent listlessness, brought to God.

passages.text: Consider my affliction and my travail. Forgive all my sins.

entries.voice: There’s nothing left to hope for.
entries.situation: Restlessness draining your hope.

passages.text: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

entries.voice: Why praise God? Nothing’s happening.
entries.situation: Grumbling that silences your praise.

passages.text: I will bless the LORD at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth.

entries.voice: This way of life is too hard. No one could keep it up.
entries.situation: Hope fading as the life of faith looks unbearably hard.

passages.text: Trust in the LORD, and do good. Dwell in the land, and enjoy safe pasture.

entries.voice: Move somewhere else. Anywhere would be better.
entries.situation: The restless urge to move to a new place.

passages.text: Wait for the LORD, and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you shall see it.

entries.voice: When I pray, everything feels dim and unsteady.
entries.situation: Restlessness clouding your mind’s clarity in prayer.
entries.note: Evagrius once asked John of Thebes where the light seen in prayer comes from. Only God’s grace can illumine the mind, John answered.

passages.text: My heart throbs. My strength fails me. As for the light of my eyes, it has also left me.

entries.voice: Even the angels have stepped away from me.
entries.situation: Feeling left alone and exposed to temptation.

passages.text: My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my plague. My kinsmen stand far away. They also who seek after my life lay snares. Those who seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and meditate deceits all day long.

greek.text: My friends and my neighbours drew near before me, and stood still; and my nearest of kin stood afar off. While they pressed hard upon me that sought my soul: and they that sought my hurt spoke vanities, and devised deceits all the day.

entries.voice: You’ve waited long enough. God isn’t going to answer.
entries.situation: Losing patience while waiting for God’s mercy.

passages.text: I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me, and heard my cry.

entries.voice: Crying won’t do any good.
entries.situation: Doubting the value of tears in a time of struggle.

passages.text: My tears have been my food day and night, while they continually ask me, “Where is your God?”

entries.voice: Everything feels gray and sad.
entries.situation: Restlessness sliding into sadness.
entries.note: Elsewhere Evagrius advises dividing the soul in two, one part comforting the other, using exactly this verse.

passages.text: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.

greek.text: Wherefore art thou very sad, O my soul? and wherefore dost thou trouble me? hope in God; for I will give thanks to him; he is the salvation of my countenance.

entries.voice: It’s fighting me all day long.
entries.situation: All-day restlessness and struggle, brought to God.

passages.text: Be merciful to me, God, for man wants to swallow me up. All day long, he attacks and oppresses me.

entries.voice: The anger and the cravings have finally gone quiet.
entries.situation: Thanksgiving when anger and desire let go of you.

passages.text: You allowed men to ride over our heads. We went through fire and through water, but you brought us to the place of abundance.

entries.voice: They got promoted and became powerful. And me?
entries.situation: Restless envy when a peer or relative gets ahead.

passages.text: But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.

entries.voice: Go visit someone. You need cheering up.
entries.situation: Escaping restlessness by looking for distraction in company.

passages.text: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted. I remember God, and I groan. I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed.

greek.text: In the day of mine affliction I earnestly sought the Lord; even with my hands by night before him, and I was not deceived; my soul refused to be comforted. I remembered God, and rejoiced; I poured out my complaint, and my soul fainted.

entries.voice: Years and years of this miserable life stretch ahead.
entries.situation: Dreading a long, dreary future.

passages.text: As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.

entries.voice: This place is unhealthy. You need a new one.
entries.situation: Finding fault with where you live as an excuse to move.

passages.text: “This is my resting place forever. I will live here, for I have desired it.

greek.text: This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have chosen it.

entries.voice: My thoughts hound me and frighten me.
entries.situation: Persecuting, frightening thoughts, brought to God.

passages.text: For the enemy pursues my soul. He has struck my life down to the ground. He has made me live in dark places, as those who have been long dead. Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate.

entries.voice: Lean back and nap. The work can wait.
entries.situation: Dodging work and drifting into sleep.

passages.text: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep? A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep— so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.

entries.voice: Skip the hard parts of obeying God.
entries.situation: Neglecting the effort that faithfulness takes.

entries.voice: There’s no love in this community. Nobody comforts anyone.
entries.situation: Complaining about others as an excuse to pull away.

passages.text: A man who isolates himself pursues selfishness, and defies all sound judgment.

greek.text: A man who wishes to separate from friends seeks excuses; but at all times he will be liable to reproach.

entries.voice: This restlessness makes me so sad.
entries.situation: Saddened by a season of listlessness.

passages.text: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty. For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole. He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.

greek.text: But blessed is the man whom the Lord has reproved; and reject not thou the chastening of the Almighty. For he causes a man to be in pain, and restores him again: he smites, and his hands heal. Six times he shall deliver thee out of distresses: and in the seventh harm shall not touch thee.

entries.voice: Old age, poverty and disease are all waiting for you.
entries.situation: Picturing a long, lonely, sick old age.

passages.text: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers. (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)

entries.voice: Somewhere else, life would be easier and you could help more people.
entries.situation: Imagining an easier, more fruitful life in another place.

passages.text: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort, before I go where I will not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death…

greek.text: Is not the time of my life short? suffer me to rest a little, before I go whence I shall not return, to a land of darkness and gloominess; to a land of perpetual darkness, where there is no light, neither can any one see the life of mortals.

entries.voice: Nobody sees what I’m going through.
entries.situation: Feeling that your struggle is invisible.

passages.text: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’

greek.text: For thou shouldest not say, There shall be no visitation of a man, whereas there is a visitation on him from the Lord.

entries.voice: People in the world have it good. Lucky them.
entries.situation: Envying people whose lives revolve around the world.

passages.text: Indeed all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.

entries.voice: I’m sick, and I’ve lost all will to keep going.
entries.situation: Illness bringing on listlessness.

passages.text: I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and executes judgment for me. He will bring me out to the light. I will see his righteousness.

entries.voice: I’m so sluggish I can barely move.
entries.situation: Crushed under sloth and listlessness, crying out.

passages.text: Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and shall perish.

entries.voice: I’m worn out, weepy, and out of hope.
entries.situation: Exhausted and tearful after a long season of listlessness.

passages.text: The LORD says: “Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears, for your work will be rewarded,” says the LORD. “They will come again from the land of the enemy. There is hope for your latter end,” says the LORD. “Your children will come again to their own territory.

entries.voice: Take a break. Go home for a while.
entries.situation: Restlessness pushing you to take a long break from your commitments.

passages.text: Though our iniquities testify against us, work for your name’s sake, LORD; for our rebellions are many. We have sinned against you. You hope of Israel, its Savior in the time of trouble, why should you be as a foreigner in the land, and as a wayfaring man who turns aside to stay for a night?

entries.voice: This life is all hardship and labor.
entries.situation: Focusing only on how hard the life of faith is.

passages.text: The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him. It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.

entries.voice: You could be just as holy without all this commitment.
entries.situation: Thinking you can grow without the yoke of commitment.

passages.text: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth. Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he has laid it on him. Let him put his mouth in the dust, if it is so that there may be hope. Let him give his cheek to him who strikes him. Let him be filled full of reproach. For the Lord will not cast off forever.

entries.voice: This restlessness has grown too strong for me.
entries.situation: Overpowered by listlessness and crying out for mercy.

passages.text: Don’t utterly deliver us up, for your name’s sake. Don’t annul your covenant. Don’t cause your mercy to depart from us, for the sake of Abraham who is loved by you, and for the sake of Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one,

entries.voice: Go visit your father. It’s your duty.
entries.situation: Using family duty as an exit from your calling.
entries.note: Evagrius wrote for monks who had left home. The thought uses a real duty as a way out of a calling.

passages.text: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”

entries.voice: I want to go back to my family.
entries.situation: Longing to return to the relatives you left.

passages.text: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.

entries.voice: Surely Jesus doesn’t ask me to put him above my family.
entries.situation: Struggling with Christ’s call to love him above family.

passages.text: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

entries.voice: Your family says you only turned to God because you failed.
entries.situation: Stung by relatives who question your motives for faith.

passages.text: But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than men.

entries.voice: With all these troubles, why bother?
entries.situation: Hardship breeding listlessness.

passages.text: rejoicing in hope, enduring in troubles, continuing steadfastly in prayer,

entries.voice: Complain. Things are terrible here.
entries.situation: Restlessness turning into grumbling.

passages.text: Don’t grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.

entries.voice: No one has suffered the way I’m suffering.
entries.situation: Sad, and forgetting what others like Paul endured.

passages.text: …in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, and in deaths often. Five times I received forty stripes minus one from the Jews. Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I have been a night and a day in the deep. I have been in travels often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers; in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness. …

entries.voice: Why be grateful for these people?
entries.situation: Unthankful for the community and mentors around you.

passages.text: giving thanks always concerning all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father; subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Christ.

entries.voice: Suffering for Christ is just a burden.
entries.situation: Not seeing that suffering for Christ is a gift.

passages.text: Because it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf, having the same conflict which you saw in me and now hear is in me.

entries.voice: Give it up. Walk away from this path.
entries.situation: Wanting to abandon your path and your place.

passages.text: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise. “In a very little while, he who comes will come and will not wait. But the righteous one will live by faith. If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.”

entries.voice: Go back to the city and see everyone you love.
entries.situation: Longing for the city and your old life.

passages.text: For we don’t have here an enduring city, but we seek that which is to come.

entries.voice: I’m being punished. That’s why I feel like this.
entries.situation: Believing your heaviness is a punishment.

passages.text: Others were tried by mocking and scourging, yes, moreover by bonds and imprisonment. They were stoned. They were sawn apart. They were tempted. They were slain with the sword. They went around in sheep skins and in goat skins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated— of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves, and the holes of the earth.

entries.voice: The leaders here are cold. Why listen to them?
entries.situation: Fed up with your leaders and unwilling to follow them.

passages.text: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch on behalf of your souls, as those who will give account, that they may do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.

entries.voice: This heaviness has changed me for the worse.
entries.situation: Saddened by how long listlessness has lingered.

passages.text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

entries.voice: I keep bouncing from place to place and person to person.
entries.situation: Restlessly driven from place to place, worn out and humiliated.

passages.text: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.

entries.voice: Go back out there and teach your family. They need you.
entries.situation: Leaving your calling too soon with the excuse of helping others.

passages.text: It came to pass, when they had taken them out, that he said, “Escape for your life! Don’t look behind you, and don’t stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountains, lest you be consumed!”

entries.voice: Why do they get that gift and not me?
entries.situation: Jealousy of someone else’s spiritual gifts or insight.

passages.text: Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!”

entries.voice: I should be ordained, or put in charge.
entries.situation: Wanting a sacred role out of vanity, blind to its dangers.
entries.note: The bronze censers of Korah’s followers, who seized the priesthood for themselves, were hammered into a warning for Israel.

passages.text: Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers which those who were burned had offered; and they beat them out for a covering of the altar, to be a memorial to the children of Israel, to the end that no stranger who isn’t of the offspring of Aaron, would come near to burn incense before the LORD, that he not be as Korah and as his company; as the LORD spoke to him by Moses.

entries.voice: Do the right thing where people can see it.
entries.situation: Doing good mainly to be noticed.

passages.text: You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live and inherit the land which the LORD your God gives you.

entries.voice: Mention your fasting. Casually.
entries.situation: Mixing talk of your spiritual efforts with a desire for admiration.
entries.note: Evagrius pictures vanity yoked to talk of one’s disciplines, like an ox and a donkey pulling one plow.

passages.text: You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.

greek.text: Thou shalt not plough with an ox and an ass together.

entries.voice: Look how respected you are here.
entries.situation: Savoring your standing in other people’s eyes.

passages.text: Saul’s servants spoke those words in the ears of David. David said, “Does it seem to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-law, since I am a poor man and little known?”

entries.voice: I can’t leave. What would people think?
entries.situation: Staying in an unhealthy place because leaving would hurt your image.

passages.text: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “See now, the place where we live and meet with you is too small for us. Please let us go to the Jordan, and each man take a beam from there, and let’s make us a place there, where we may live.” He answered, “Go!”

entries.voice: Those voices promised me a high position. Maybe they’re right.
entries.situation: Believing flattering promises of status.

passages.text: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth. Their heart is destruction. Their throat is an open tomb. They flatter with their tongue.

entries.voice: Start teaching everyone. You’re ready.
entries.situation: Rushing to teach before your own soul is healthy.
entries.note: Evagrius reads the sparrow’s nest beside God’s altar as staying put until you are grown.

passages.text: Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King, and my God.

entries.voice: Imagine yourself in charge, managing everything.
entries.situation: Daydreams of being in charge that scatter your mind.

passages.text: Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God.

entries.voice: Cut yourself off from them. They’re only leading you astray.
entries.situation: Withdrawing from your community out of a sense of superiority.

passages.text: The proud have hidden a snare for me, they have spread the cords of a net by the path. They have set traps for me.

entries.voice: Weigh in on everything. People want your opinion.
entries.situation: Talking too much and getting involved in other people’s disputes.

passages.text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.

entries.voice: Lead them now. You don’t need to wait.
entries.situation: Taking charge of others before you are grounded.

passages.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

entries.voice: You haven’t mastered Scripture, so why keep at it?
entries.situation: Giving up on Scripture because you can’t master it quickly.

passages.text: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.

entries.voice: You’re young, but you don’t need a mentor.
entries.situation: Young and eager to go it alone without guidance.

passages.text: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.

greek.text: A youth when in company with a godly man, will be restrained in his devices, and then his way will be straight.

entries.voice: Cosign the loan. They’ll love you for it.
entries.situation: Taking on other people’s debts to be liked or admired.

passages.text: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts. If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

greek.text: Become not surety from respect of a man's person. For if those have not whence to give compensation, they will take the bed that is under thee.

entries.voice: Tell them the deep things. They’ll be impressed.
entries.situation: Sharing sacred or personal things to impress people who won’t value them.

passages.text: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

entries.voice: Go out where people can see you. It’ll inspire them.
entries.situation: Seeking visibility under the guise of being an example.

passages.text: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.

greek.text: The words of cunning knaves are soft; but they smite even to the inmost parts of the bowels.

entries.voice: Bring on the big battles. Imagine the glory of winning.
entries.situation: Inviting great trials so you can be admired for surviving them.
entries.note: Evagrius learned from John of Thebes that the demon does this out of vainglory.

passages.text: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart. When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

greek.text: A weeping enemy promises all things with his lips, but in his heart he contrives deceit. Though thine enemy intreat thee with a loud voice, consent not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.

entries.voice: Let them know how disciplined you are.
entries.situation: Making sure others hear about your good habits.

passages.text: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

entries.voice: Speak up now. Stay quiet then. Whatever looks best.
entries.situation: Letting vanity decide when you speak and when you stay silent.

passages.text: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

entries.voice: Surely no one is watching how I serve God.
entries.situation: Forgetting that the enemy notices your service and will test your motives.

passages.text: Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing? Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

entries.voice: I’ll make you famous everywhere.
entries.situation: Promises of fame that pose as help.

passages.text: Therefore the Lord, GOD of Armies, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.

greek.text: but the Lord of hosts shall send dishonour upon thine honour, and burning fire shall be kindled upon thy glory.

entries.voice: People’s praise matters more to me than knowing Christ.
entries.situation: Loving human glory more than the knowledge of Christ.

passages.text: The voice of one saying, “Cry out!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. The grass withers, the flower fades, because the LORD’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass. The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”

entries.voice: I can’t stop wanting recognition, and I’m already hurting.
entries.situation: A persistent longing for glory, on top of anger and sadness.

passages.text: Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved; for you are my praise.

entries.voice: That dream means you’ll be a leader. People will come.
entries.situation: Reading dreams as signs of your coming importance.

passages.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.

greek.text: and laid a stone upon me.

entries.voice: You’re so spiritual you’ll be taken up to heaven.
entries.situation: Inflated spiritual experiences that lead to a fall.
entries.note: Evagrius says some who believed this were shipwrecked.

passages.text: And Daniel said, “You have certainly lied against your own head; for even now the angel of God has received the sentence of God and will cut you in two.”

entries.voice: Your wisdom will make you famous among the powerful.
entries.situation: Dreaming of influence with important people.

passages.text: Then Daniel said to him, “You have also certainly lied against your own head; for the angel of God waits with the sword to cut you in two, that he may destroy you.”

entries.voice: Teach it first. You can practice it later.
entries.situation: Wanting to teach what you don’t yet do.

passages.text: Therefore, whoever shall break one of these least commandments and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.voice: Make sure they see you giving.
entries.situation: Piety performed for an audience.

passages.text: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

entries.voice: Picture yourself praying. Don’t you look holy?
entries.situation: Imagining how you look while you pray.
entries.note: Evagrius notes that the mind at prayer has no shape. Picturing yourself praying is vainglory at work.

passages.text: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.

entries.voice: Look a little tired. Let them guess you’re fasting.
entries.situation: Letting people know about your fasting or sacrifices.

passages.text: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.

entries.voice: Keep chatting. Words don’t matter.
entries.situation: Empty talk that pulls your mind into distraction.

passages.text: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

entries.voice: Look how spiritually powerful you’ve become!
entries.situation: Pride in spiritual victories instead of joy in God’s grace.

passages.text: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

entries.voice: You have a real gift for healing.
entries.situation: Flattering thoughts about your spiritual gifts.

passages.text: …When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.

entries.voice: Pay your way into the position.
entries.situation: Trying to buy influence or a role.

passages.text: But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!

entries.voice: Master the world’s learning. Then they’ll respect you.
entries.situation: Craving intellectual prestige.

passages.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in their craftiness.”

entries.voice: Brag a little about how steady you’ve been.
entries.situation: Boasting about your faithfulness and hard work.

passages.text: But “he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.” For it isn’t he who commends himself who is approved, but whom the Lord commends.

entries.voice: Convince your relatives you’re on the right path.
entries.situation: Needing your family’s approval for your spiritual life.

passages.text: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn’t be a servant of Christ.

entries.voice: Do something impressive so they’ll choose you.
entries.situation: Maneuvering to be chosen for an honored role.

passages.text: Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.

entries.voice: You should be teaching others by now.
entries.situation: Wanting to teach before you’re grounded in the truth.

passages.text: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment. For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.

entries.voice: Ask God for impressive gifts.
entries.situation: Asking for spiritual gifts so others will admire you.

passages.text: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

entries.voice: Look at the glory the world offers.
entries.situation: Dazzled by worldly glory.

passages.text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him.

entries.voice: I’m the Lord’s holy one.
entries.situation: Thinking of yourself as specially holy.
entries.note: Evagrius answers this boast with God’s curse on the serpent, the first proud one.

passages.text: The LORD God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

entries.voice: You’re pure now. Impure thoughts don’t touch you anymore.
entries.situation: Pride in your own purity.

passages.text: Abraham answered, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord, although I am dust and ashes.

entries.voice: God doesn’t provide for me. I take care of myself.
entries.situation: Denying God’s care and the help he sends.

passages.text: He blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day, the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Let them grow into a multitude upon the earth.”

entries.voice: Why does studying spiritual things always meet resistance?
entries.situation: Wondering why time with God’s word gets crowded out.
entries.note: Pharaoh’s strategy was to pile on more work so the people had no time for words of hope. Evagrius sees the same tactic used against those who study God’s word.

passages.text: Let heavier work be laid on the men, that they may labor in it. Don’t let them pay any attention to lying words.”

greek.text: Let the works of these men be made grievous, and let them care for these things, and not care for vain words.

entries.voice: You don’t need God to save you.
entries.situation: Rejecting the salvation by which every other temptation is overcome.

passages.text: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD, and said, “I will sing to the LORD, for he has triumphed gloriously. He has thrown the horse and his rider into the sea. The LORD is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

entries.voice: I beat my sadness by my own strength.
entries.situation: Taking the credit for coming through a dark season.

passages.text: Your right hand, LORD, is glorious in power. Your right hand, LORD, dashes the enemy in pieces. In the greatness of your excellency, you overthrow those who rise up against you. You send out your wrath. It consumes them as stubble.

greek.text: Thy right hand, O God, has been glorified in strength; thy right hand, O God, has broken the enemies. And in the abundance of thy glory thou hast broken the adversaries to pieces: thou sentest forth thy wrath, it devoured them as stubble.

entries.voice: I don’t need any guidance. Nobody can teach me.
entries.situation: Scorning the help and correction God sends.

passages.text: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared. Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. Don’t provoke him, for he will not pardon your disobedience, for my name is in him.

entries.voice: Those elders haven’t done any more than I have.
entries.situation: Looking down on spiritual elders and mentors.

passages.text: “‘You shall rise up before the gray head and honor the face of the elderly; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

entries.voice: Curse God. Say it.
entries.situation: A blasphemous thought pushing your mind toward ruin.
entries.note: Unwanted blasphemous thoughts are a common temptation. Having one is not the same as choosing it. Evagrius answers the thought instead of obeying it.

passages.text: …Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin. …

greek.text: And speak to the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say to them, Whosoever shall curse God shall bear his sin. And he that names the name of the Lord, let him die the death: let all the congregation of Israel stone him with stones; whether he be a stranger or a native, let him die for naming the name of the Lord.

entries.voice: Blasphemous thoughts keep coming, and I can’t pray freely.
entries.situation: Persistent blasphemous thoughts robbing your prayer of confidence.

passages.text: When the ark went forward, Moses said, “Rise up, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you flee before you!”

entries.voice: Knowing Christ and keeping his commands isn’t worth much.
entries.situation: Belittling the beauty of knowing Christ.

passages.text: …The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceedingly good land. If the LORD delights in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us: a land which flows with milk and honey. Only don’t rebel against the LORD, neither fear the people of the land; for they are bread for us. Their defense is removed from over them, and the LORD is with us. Don’t fear them.”

entries.voice: Is God even in you? Test him and find out.
entries.situation: Doubting God’s presence and wanting to put him to the test.

passages.text: You shall not tempt the LORD your God, as you tempted him in Massah.

entries.voice: I beat these temptations by my own power.
entries.situation: Supposing your own strength defeated what was against you.

passages.text: and lest you say in your heart, “My power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth.” But you shall remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he swore to your fathers, as it is today.

entries.voice: I won because I’m righteous.
entries.situation: Believing your goodness earned you victory and understanding.

passages.text: Don’t say in your heart, after the LORD your God has thrust them out from before you, “For my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land;” because the LORD drives them out before you because of the wickedness of these nations. Not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart do you go in to possess their land; but for the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God does drive them out from before you, and that he may establish the word which the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

entries.voice: Everyone praises you. You’re the father of the wise.
entries.situation: Flattering thoughts of universal admiration.

passages.text: You will be cursed in the city, and you will be cursed in the field. Your basket and your kneading trough will be cursed.

entries.voice: You have no free will, so none of it is your fault.
entries.situation: Denying free will to escape responsibility for sin.

passages.text: Behold, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil.

entries.voice: That vision must be from God.
entries.situation: Trusting every spiritual experience without discernment.
entries.note: Evagrius’s test: a true messenger from God may startle you at first, but leaves joy and deep peace. A false one leaves fear and agitation.

passages.text: When Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man stood in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him and said to him, “Are you for us, or for our enemies?” He said, “No; but I have come now as commander of the LORD’s army.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and worshiped, and asked him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”

entries.voice: You don’t need God’s grace.
entries.situation: Denying your need for grace.

passages.text: If one man sins against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, they didn’t listen to the voice of their father, because the LORD intended to kill them.

entries.voice: These thoughts stop my prayer, so I’ll get on my knees.
entries.situation: Answering blasphemous thoughts by kneeling in humble prayer.

passages.text: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he bowed himself down on the earth, and put his face between his knees.

entries.voice: These frightening blasphemies shake me so much I can’t pray.
entries.situation: Shaken by frightening blasphemous thoughts and losing confidence in prayer.

passages.text: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: ‘The LORD says, “Don’t be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”

entries.voice: Unspeakable words against God keep rising in me.
entries.situation: Horrified by blasphemies that seem to speak inside you.
entries.note: Evagrius recommends fasting and reading Scripture during this temptation.

passages.text: Hezekiah prayed before the LORD, and said, “LORD, the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. Incline your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.

entries.voice: The victory was mine, not God’s.
entries.situation: Denying that victory comes from God.

passages.text: and said, “From you comes victory. From you comes wisdom. Yours is the glory, and I am your servant. Blessed are you, who have given me wisdom. I give thanks to you, O Lord of our fathers.

entries.voice: These blasphemous thoughts just won’t leave.
entries.situation: Persistent blasphemous thoughts, brought to God.

passages.text: LORD, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me, lest they tear apart my soul like a lion, ripping it in pieces, while there is no one to deliver.

entries.voice: Something proud and dazzling is coming at me.
entries.situation: Pride arriving disguised as something bright and good.

passages.text: Don’t let the foot of pride come against me. Don’t let the hand of the wicked drive me away.

entries.voice: My own skill won this.
entries.situation: Crediting a victory to your own ability instead of God’s help.

passages.text: For I will not trust in my bow, neither will my sword save me. But you have saved us from our adversaries, and have shamed those who hate us.

entries.voice: I’ll explain the Scriptures to you myself.
entries.situation: Self-appointed spiritual teaching that is really deception.
entries.note: Evagrius says Macarius answered such a demon with this verse.

passages.text: But to the wicked God says, “What right do you have to declare my statutes, that you have taken my covenant on your lips, since you hate instruction, and throw my words behind you?

entries.voice: Proud thoughts are crowding in from every side.
entries.situation: Pride closing in on your mind.

passages.text: How long will you assault a man? Would all of you throw him down, like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?

entries.voice: My pride makes it hard to pray honestly.
entries.situation: Persistent pride stealing your openness in prayer.

passages.text: Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions.

greek.text: The words of transgressors have overpowered us; but do thou pardon our sins.

entries.voice: Say something unspeakable about God.
entries.situation: Blasphemous words rising in your mind.

passages.text: Don’t lift up your horn on high. Don’t speak with a stiff neck.”

entries.voice: Look how much I’ve built up in other people’s lives.
entries.situation: Pride in your spiritual influence on others.

passages.text: Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.

entries.voice: They’re slacking. Not like me.
entries.situation: Mocking others for neglecting their faith.

passages.text: Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.

greek.text: The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble.

entries.voice: What feeds the evil that fights me?
entries.situation: Wanting to understand what the forces of evil feed on.

passages.text: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.

greek.text: For these live upon the bread of ungodliness, and are drunken with wine of transgression.

entries.voice: Why visit them? They don’t know any more than you.
entries.situation: Avoiding fellowship because you think you know better.

passages.text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

entries.voice: Don’t ask anyone to pray for you. You can handle this.
entries.situation: Too proud to ask others for prayer during a long trial.

passages.text: A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city. Disputes are like the bars of a fortress.

greek.text: A brother helped by a brother is as a strong and high city; and is as strong as a well-founded palace.

entries.voice: You’re pure and victorious.
entries.situation: Believing you are clean and without sin.

passages.text: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I am clean and without sin”?

entries.voice: Holy fear? You’ve outgrown it. You’ve succeeded.
entries.situation: Treating reverent fear as something only for the unsuccessful.

passages.text: Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.

entries.voice: My background makes me better than them.
entries.situation: Pride in your family, birth or background.

passages.text: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.

entries.voice: Look at all their sins.
entries.situation: Fixating on other people’s sins.

passages.text: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn’t sin.

entries.voice: You’ve arrived. You’re a mature believer now.
entries.situation: Believing you’ve reached spiritual maturity.

passages.text: For to him who is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

entries.voice: You’re so humble you could stand to be a little proud.
entries.situation: Being “cured” of humility by bad advice.

passages.text: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.

greek.text: But ye are all bad physicians, and healers of diseases.

entries.voice: Say what you really think about God.
entries.situation: Thoughts that try to drag your mind into blasphemy.

passages.text: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?

greek.text: Do ye not speak before the Lord, and utter deceit before him?

entries.voice: Let me remind you of what they’ve done wrong.
entries.situation: Mentally listing other people’s sins.

passages.text: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one. Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass.

greek.text: For who shall be pure from uncleanness? not even one; if even his life should be but one day upon the earth: and his months are numbered by him: thou hast appointed him for a time, and he shall by no means exceed it.

entries.voice: God must be very pleased with my way of life.
entries.situation: Pride in your life as an offering to God.

passages.text: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him that you make your ways perfect?

greek.text: For what matters it to the Lord, if thou wert blameless in thy works? or is it profitable that thou shouldest perfect thy way?

entries.voice: Rise up against heaven itself.
entries.situation: A thought that pushes you toward open rebellion against God.

passages.text: The LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, Satan! Yes, the LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”

entries.voice: You’re so wise.
entries.situation: Pride in your own wisdom.

passages.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!

entries.voice: Nothing frightens the enemy.
entries.situation: Not believing that knowing Christ exposes and terrifies evil.

passages.text: The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it will be afraid, because of the plans of the LORD of Armies, which he determines against it.

greek.text: And the land of the Jews shall be for a terror to the Egyptians: whosoever shall name it to them, they shall fear, because of the counsel which the Lord of hosts has purposed concerning it.

entries.voice: These powers are like gods. Fear them.
entries.situation: Giving evil powers a godlike place in your mind.

passages.text: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’”

entries.voice: Look, you’ve beaten your enemies.
entries.situation: Pride in your victories.

passages.text: LORD, I know that the way of man is not in himself. It is not in man who walks to direct his steps.

entries.voice: I had a blasphemous thought, and I’m crushed by it.
entries.situation: Saddened and ashamed after a blasphemous thought.
entries.note: A thought that horrifies you is not one you have chosen. God “does not afflict willingly.”

passages.text: For the Lord will not cast off forever. For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses. For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.

greek.text: For the Lord will not reject for ever. For he that has brought down will pity, and that according to the abundance of his mercy. He has not answered in anger from his heart, though he has brought low the children of a man.

entries.voice: Blasphemies cloud my mind just when I pray.
entries.situation: Blasphemous thoughts covering your mind at prayer.

passages.text: “You have covered us with anger and pursued us. You have killed. You have not pitied. You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through. You have made us an off-scouring and refuse in the middle of the peoples.

greek.text: Thou hast visited us in wrath, and driven us away: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied. Thou hast veiled thyself with a cloud because of prayer, that I might be blind, and be cast off. Ain. Thou hast set us alone in the midst of the nations.

entries.voice: You should be first among them.
entries.situation: Wanting to be first in your community.

passages.text: He sat down and called the twelve; and he said to them, “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”

entries.voice: You’ve done what’s required. That’s plenty.
entries.situation: Thinking you’ve done enough for God.

passages.text: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”

entries.voice: I’m in the right. Their weak efforts don’t impress me.
entries.situation: Justifying yourself and looking down on other people’s weaker efforts.

passages.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

entries.voice: They only fast because they’re too weak to handle food.
entries.situation: Despising someone who practices a discipline you don’t.

passages.text: Don’t let him who eats despise him who doesn’t eat. …

entries.voice: They eat because they have no self-control.
entries.situation: Judging someone who doesn’t keep your discipline.

passages.text: …Don’t let him who doesn’t eat judge him who eats, for God has accepted him.

entries.voice: I’ve conquered my appetite and my temper.
entries.situation: Pride in your self-mastery.

passages.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

entries.voice: Anything that looks bright and wise must be true.
entries.situation: Not believing evil can disguise itself as a teacher of truth.

passages.text: And no wonder, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light. It is no great thing therefore if his servants also masquerade as servants of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.

entries.voice: They fell. How pathetic.
entries.situation: Despising those who stumble.

passages.text: Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.

entries.voice: You’ve reached perfection.
entries.situation: Believing you’ve arrived in obeying God.

passages.text: Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect; but I press on, that I may take hold of that for which also I was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.

entries.voice: There’s no sin left in your heart.
entries.situation: Pride that says you have no sin.

passages.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

entries.voice: Can I trust myself to stay faithful to the end?
entries.situation: Learning to rely on God, not yourself, to keep you to the end.

passages.text: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy, to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.
